teaching_blocks.title: Train, Evaluate and Persist Weights
teaching_blocks.content: Validation should use the supplied evaluation behavior without updating parameters. Two separate controls are needed: the model's layer mode and whether tensor operations record a gradient graph. One does not substitute for the other.

teaching_blocks.title: The working rule
teaching_blocks.content: Use model.train() during parameter training and model.eval() during validation; the mode changes behavior of layers such as dropout and batch normalization. Wrap validation prediction in with torch.no_grad(): to disable graph recording and avoid building gradients for validation. Evaluation mode and no_grad serve different purposes: eval changes relevant layer behavior, while no_grad controls gradient recording.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Keep validation as a forward-only pass without optimizer.step(), then restore model.train() before the next training pass. Write assert predicate checks for the declared valid, boundary and failure cases; a false predicate raises AssertionError during ordinary non-optimized execution. For the mode-sensitive fixture, import torch and nn from torch and construct nn.Dropout with p=0.5. During training, each element is randomly zeroed with probability p; retained values are scaled by 1/(1-p). During evaluation the layer returns x unchanged. Assert the evaluation identity and training masking/scaling rule without assuming every random call masks an element. torch.no_grad disables gradient recording but does not switch dropout to evaluation mode.

teaching_blocks.title: A bounded work example
teaching_blocks.content:
For a dropout fixture with p=0.5, training randomly masks elements and doubles retained values. Evaluation returns the input unchanged. Test the masking/scaling rule without assuming every random training call must mask at least one element. Wrap validation in no_grad and set eval; a no_grad-only training-mode dropout fixture can still use dropout behavior. Keep validation forward-only, with no optimizer step, and restore train before the next training pass. This makes the fixture demonstrate why an evaluation-mode switch and a gradient-recording switch address different concerns. Compare expected evaluation output and the permitted training outcomes, not one arbitrarily expected random mask.

Training mode and gradient recording can be considered independently in the fixture. Evaluation-mode dropout behaves as an identity even if graph recording is enabled. Training-mode dropout can still mask values while no_grad is active. Neither observation alone describes the whole validation procedure, which also excludes parameter updates. Inspect the layer output and the chosen context separately, then restore training mode before returning to the training loop. This avoids interpreting a stochastic dropout value as a prediction-quality problem or assuming that a disabled graph has also changed layer behavior.

Put the restored model in evaluation mode. On a fixed order fixture, compare original and restored evaluation predictions under the declared tolerances. The state mapping and prediction fixture provide complementary checks. Binary file handles are required for the specified save/load path. teaching_blocks.title: Stop and Debug Training
teaching_blocks.content: A validation quantity improves and then stalls. Early stopping is a predeclared controller over this sequence, not a decision to use whichever epoch happened to run last. Preserve the best checkpoint accepted under the declared minimum-improvement rule while training can still alter live parameters.

teaching_blocks.title: The working rule
teaching_blocks.content: Predeclare the validation quantity, improvement direction, minimum improvement and patience; patience counts consecutive epochs without sufficient improvement. For a minimized validation quantity, reset the non-improvement counter only when current < best − min_delta; otherwise increment it and stop when the declared patience is exhausted. Here, best is the validation value at the most recent checkpoint accepted under min_delta, not necessarily the lowest observed value. Retain that accepted checkpoint’s model weights rather than automatically using the last epoch’s weights.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: A state_dict refers to live parameter values, so preserve a best-epoch state with a deep copy or a saved state file before later updates alter the model. Do not use protected test observations to fit preprocessing, choose a model or tune its settings; doing so leaks information into the chosen system. Implement the controller as a while loop bounded by maximum epochs and the non-improvement rule; update best loss/checkpoint inside the improvement branch and use break when patience is exhausted.

teaching_blocks.title: A bounded work example
teaching_blocks.content:
Suppose minimized validation values are 0.50, 0.44, 0.43 and 0.45, with min_delta 0.02 and patience 2. The move from 0.50 to 0.44 is sufficient improvement and resets the counter. The value 0.43 does not satisfy 0.43 < 0.44−0.02, so the counter becomes one; 0.45 makes it two and exhausts patience. The lowest observed value is 0.43, but the best checkpoint accepted under min_delta is the one at 0.44. Retain the 0.44 checkpoint’s weights, preserving them by deep copy or a saved state file. Bound the while loop by maximum epochs as well as the non-improvement rule. Protected-test observations do not decide patience or checkpoint choice.

Trace the controller's counter explicitly after every validation value. Reset only when the minimized quantity improves by more than min_delta, increment otherwise and stop when patience is exhausted or the epoch bound is reached. The fixture's small decrease from 0.44 to 0.43 is intentionally insufficient under the declared 0.02 rule. Save or deep-copy the 0.44 checkpoint’s weights when that qualifying improvement is accepted. This separates controller state from the live model state that later epochs can change. Restore that saved checkpoint for subsequent use rather than the last weights merely because they were the most recently trained.

The identical rerun is what makes the correction test informative. Preserve the fixture, target contract and baseline failing evidence while changing the one supported factor. teaching_blocks.title: Profile and Choose Training Hardware
teaching_blocks.content: The order-training run is slow, but a duration alone does not identify where time goes. Mark data-loading and model-computation regions and inspect the supplied profiler evidence before choosing one bottleneck change.

teaching_blocks.title: The working rule
teaching_blocks.content: Wrap the measured computation in the PyTorch profiler context and mark data-loading and model-computation regions with record_function labels. Inspect key_averages().table(...) or the trace to attribute elapsed operator and labeled-region work to the observed bottleneck. Warm up the workload before comparing steady-state execution and remove profiler overhead when making the final unprofiled timing comparison.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: CUDA work is asynchronous, so CPU clock timings require synchronization at the measurement boundaries to include completed accelerator work. Change one supported bottleneck factor and compare the same bounded workload again rather than inferring improvement only from a code change. Inspect CPU and memory measurements and running process state during the profiled interval, using docker stats and docker top for a containerized run, to distinguish resource limits from stage timing evidence.

teaching_blocks.title: A bounded work example
teaching_blocks.content:
Warm up the bounded workload, then profile its labeled regions. If the trace attributes most measured work to loading, test one supported loading factor rather than immediately changing model computation. Inspect CPU, memory and process state during the same interval; for the container fixture, docker stats and docker top provide that supporting evidence. After the change, compare the same bounded workload again without profiler overhead in the final timing. On CUDA, synchronize measurement boundaries so a CPU clock includes completed accelerator work. Keep the profiling attribution separate from the final unprofiled performance comparison, since they answer related but different questions.

The profiler trace supplies attribution, while the unprofiled rerun supplies the matched elapsed-time comparison. Keep the same bounded workload and one-factor change between those two comparisons. A loading-region label should enclose the intended loading work; a model-compute label should identify that separate work rather than blend it with setup. Runtime CPU, memory and process evidence must refer to the same window. Synchronization at accelerator timing boundaries accounts for asynchronous completion. This makes the observed difference interpretable without assuming that a profiler's overhead or a shifted measurement boundary is a genuine speed improvement.

teaching_blocks.title: A distinction to keep
teaching_blocks.content: A code change is not evidence of improvement. Asynchronous accelerator work and profiler overhead can alter timing interpretation unless the measurement boundaries and final comparison are controlled.

teaching_blocks.title: Profile and Choose Training Hardware
teaching_blocks.content: The supplied CPU and accelerator options need a matched workload comparison. Hardware selection uses completed work, quality, memory and billing scope, not the assumption that accelerator utilization is itself a cost or quality result.

teaching_blocks.title: The working rule

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Estimate compute execution cost from the measured runtime and the applicable supplied rate, retaining the billing scope rather than assuming utilization alone is cost. For an authorized supplied Compute Engine VM, gcloud compute instances start INSTANCE --zone=ZONE and gcloud compute instances stop INSTANCE --zone=ZONE change its lifecycle state; wait for the operation and inspect the resulting state. teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify

Use gcloud compute instances describe INSTANCE --zone=ZONE to inspect the instance status and identity before and after the authorized lifecycle action. Record observed memory and whether each CPU/GPU instance option completes the same bounded matrix workload within its fixed limits.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: After benchmarking both authorized options, stop both and verify their resulting lifecycle states; use measured lifecycle durations in the billing calculation.

teaching_blocks.title: A bounded work example
teaching_blocks.content: Suppose the CPU option completes the bounded workload in 60 seconds at a supplied rate of 0.01 currency units per second; its measured compute execution cost is 0.60. Check both against the task-quality and memory limits, retaining relevant movement and warm-up interpretation. Start, connect to and inspect only the authorized instances. After both measurements, stop both and verify the lifecycle states. Record lifecycle durations for billing interpretation as well as the bounded execution measurements. Persistent disks or other charges can remain even after compute stops.

teaching_blocks.title: Fine-Tune Task-Specific Weights
teaching_blocks.content: For a supplied image-classification task, adapt a compatible pretrained ViT checkpoint within a bounded supervised run. The comparison needs the original pretrained label mapping and the task-specific head mapping kept distinct.

teaching_blocks.title: The working rule
teaching_blocks.content: For the bounded ViT image-classification adaptation, import torch, nn from torch, and AutoImageProcessor, ViTForImageClassification, TrainingArguments and Trainer from transformers. Load the supplied compatible checkpoint with ViTForImageClassification.from_pretrained(checkpoint). Retain its original label mapping for the pretrained baseline before replacing the task head. Load the matching processor with AutoImageProcessor.from_pretrained(checkpoint). Calling that processor on images with return_tensors="pt" produces pixel_values; passing the resulting inputs as keyword arguments to the model yields logits through its .logits attribute. Use this same checkpoint processor for training and validation images rather than an unrelated representation. With the supplied preprocessed datasets and image collator, construct TrainingArguments with the declared output_dir, num_train_epochs, per_device_train_batch_size and learning_rate. Set eval_strategy="epoch" and remove_unused_columns=False. Construct Trainer with model, args, train_dataset, eval_dataset=validation_dataset, data_collator and processing_class=processor. Its train method executes the bounded supervised adaptation.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: For classifier-only adaptation, iterate the existing model parameters and set their requires_grad to False. Then assign a new nn.Linear(model.config.hidden_size, num_labels) to model.classifier. Set model.num_labels and model.config.num_labels to num_labels and set config.id2label and config.label2id to the task maps. The newly constructed head parameters are trainable by default. Verify that head weights change while frozen backbone values do not. Evaluate the fine-tuned task predictions on the same validation cohort as the frozen pretrained output reference, without constructing an application or using protected test data. For binary validation counts, FPR = FP/(FP+TN) conditions on actual negatives, and FNR = FN/(FN+TP) conditions on actual positives; an empty conditioning group does not yield a defined rate.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: With zero cost for correct predictions and supplied deployment class probabilities, expected error cost is P(Y=0) × FPR × cost_FP + P(Y=1) × FNR × cost_FN. Do not use protected test observations to fit preprocessing, choose a model or tune its settings; doing so leaks information into the chosen system. For a class-index task head, verify logits shape (N, C) and target shape (N,) with long indices in [0, C), where C matches the task label mapping.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Within the adaptation run, compute the task loss, backpropagate it and compare a selected head gradient with the chain-rule reference before claiming the task head receives the intended supervised update.

teaching_blocks.title: A bounded work example
teaching_blocks.content: Imagine supplied training and validation images for two task classes. Retain the original pretrained mapping for the frozen baseline, and use the same checkpoint processor for image representation. Freeze existing parameters, replace the classifier with a two-output head using the hidden width, and update num_labels and both label maps. Verify logits shape (N, 2) and long target indices in [0, 2). In the adaptation run, inspect a selected head gradient against the chain-rule reference and verify changed head weights with unchanged frozen-backbone values. Compare adapted predictions with the frozen supplied reference on the same validation cohort under fixed cost and acceptance rules. Keep protected-test data outside adaptation and selection.

teaching_blocks.title: A distinction to keep
teaching_blocks.content: Freezing the old parameters does not freeze a newly constructed head by default. A changed head without a verified target mapping or matched validation comparison is not sufficient evidence of task-specific adaptation.

teaching_blocks.title: Reproduce a Training Experiment
teaching_blocks.content: The training behavior must leave the notebook and run from a clean shell. A script entry point makes direct execution explicit while preventing ordinary imports from silently launching the training task.

teaching_blocks.title: The working rule
teaching_blocks.content: Place the executable call behind if __name__ == "__main__": so direct script execution runs the entry point and ordinary imports do not. Define the training entry function with explicit parameters and resolve its defaults and keyword overrides before training. Load the declared JSON configuration with json.load and map its fields to the training function’s arguments.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Run the saved file with python training_script.py and compare its recorded configuration and outputs with the supplied notebook behavior. From a caller, subprocess.run(["python", script_path], check=True) executes the script and raises on a nonzero exit status. Serialize a configuration or record using json.dump(record, file_handle), and recover the structured values with json.load(file_handle) rather than treating JSON text as a Python dictionary.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Call the entry function once with its default arguments and once with explicit keyword overrides; all task state must be parameters or local values rather than notebook globals. Use f-strings such as f"{parameter_name}={resolved_value}" to emit the resolved parameters and validation result for inspection. Save the script in the repository, stage it with git add SCRIPT_PATH and commit it with git commit, retaining the resulting revision.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Run the saved entry point from a clean shell process with output redirection (python training_script.py > capture.log 2>&1), then inspect the captured parameters and result.

teaching_blocks.title: A bounded work example
teaching_blocks.content: Suppose the training function has a default setting and accepts an explicit keyword override. Call both forms with task state passed as parameters, then map a decoded JSON configuration to the entry function's arguments. Place execution behind the __main__ guard, save the script in the repository and retain its committed revision. Run it in a clean subprocess, check the exit result and inspect captured resolved parameters and validation output against the supplied notebook behavior. Output redirection captures both standard output and error in the declared log. The test is not merely whether the script starts: it checks that no forgotten notebook global supplied a necessary value.

teaching_blocks.title: A distinction to keep
teaching_blocks.content: JSON text is not a Python dictionary until decoded. A clean script also must not depend on notebook globals or print defaults as though they were the resolved keyword overrides.

teaching_blocks.title: Reproduce a Training Experiment
teaching_blocks.content: A dataset name still exists, but its contents have been overwritten. Reproduction requires the recorded object generation and actual content identity, not just a path called latest.

teaching_blocks.title: The working rule
teaching_blocks.content: A mutable object name can refer to new contents after an overwrite; Object Versioning retains noncurrent versions whose identities can be selected explicitly. Retrieve a Google Cloud Storage snapshot with bucket.blob(object_name, generation=recorded_generation).download_to_filename(local_path), preserving the generation instead of resolving the current object. Use the authorized client to confirm the supplied object/version exists before recording the snapshot as available.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Compute a digest from the actual bytes, for example hashlib.sha256(data_bytes).hexdigest(), and compare it with the recorded expected content identity. Write the object name, generation and observed digest to the local snapshot record so later training can retrieve and verify the same bytes. Upload the dataset to the version-enabled bucket with bucket.blob(object_name).upload_from_filename(local_path), then inspect the created object generation and record it.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Read the local dataset through with open(path, "rb") as handle and update the SHA-256 digest from those bytes before recording the upload identity. After overwriting the mutable latest object in the test bucket, download the originally recorded generation again and compare its digest with the original snapshot digest.

teaching_blocks.title: A bounded work example
teaching_blocks.content:
Upload the supplied dataset to the version-enabled test bucket and record its created generation and the SHA-256 digest of the local bytes. Later, select that recorded generation explicitly, verify it exists and download it. Compare the downloaded bytes' digest with the expected snapshot identity. In the authorized overwrite fixture, change only the mutable latest object, then retrieve the original generation again. The observed original digest should still match the snapshot record. Keep object name, generation and digest together: the name tells you which object family, the generation selects the version, and the digest checks the bytes you actually obtained.

The overwrite test separates immutable snapshot selection from the mutable object's current state. Verify the recorded generation exists before relying on it, and check the content after retrieval rather than assuming a version-qualified request returned the expected bytes. A local digest computed before upload and a digest of the later download can be compared directly as content evidence. Keep the selected generation in the record even when both old and latest objects happen to have the same name. The test proves retrieval of the recorded fixture, not a claim that mutable names are intrinsically safe for reproduction.

teaching_blocks.content: A mutable object name is not immutable data identity. Recording a digest without verifying downloaded bytes also does not establish that the intended snapshot was retrieved.

teaching_blocks.title: Reproduce a Training Experiment
teaching_blocks.content: The run's environment record should describe what actually executed. A remembered dependency list or a typed commit label is not independent evidence of the Python runtime and repository revision used.

teaching_blocks.title: The working rule
teaching_blocks.content: Inspect the actual local repository commit using git rev-parse --verify HEAD and include that exact revision in the environment dictionary. teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify

Inspect the local HEAD, collect pinned dependency versions with pip freeze, and record sys.version and sys.executable with the supplied runtime identity. Serialize that dictionary to the declared text manifest and parse it back. Compare the parsed revision, dependency mapping and runtime identity with independently inspected values. If the manifest says revision A but HEAD is B, reject the match rather than correcting the observed revision to fit the manifest. The dependency file can be installed with pip install -r in the declared environment. Keep the saved manifest and verified values identifiable so a later reproduction can resolve the recorded context.

The parsed manifest is the artifact a later execution will read, so inspect it after serialization rather than only inspecting the in-memory dictionary that preceded writing. Compare its dependency mapping with the freeze output, its revision with HEAD and its Python/runtime fields with the actual process. Paths such as sys.executable help identify which interpreter executed, while sys.version records that interpreter's version information. Keep these values beside the environment identity instead of treating them as substitutes for it. A mismatch is a verification failure to resolve, not a reason to change the independently observed environment values.

teaching_blocks.content: Writing a manifest is not verifying it. Runtime details and dependency pins must come from the actual environment, and a parsed record with a mismatch cannot be declared accurate.

teaching_blocks.title: A bounded work example
teaching_blocks.content:

A shell pipe connects one command's output to another's input; it is not the same operation as saving both output streams to a log.

Compare captured resolved parameters with the run record as well as inspecting exit success. A process can exit successfully while using a wrong dataset or default setting, so the reproduction verdict needs identity and configuration checks too. Relative paths are interpreted from the actual working directory; navigate explicitly before invoking the recorded script. The pinned environment and recorded code commit govern which implementation runs, while the verified snapshot governs its inputs. These separate pieces make the bounded reproduction auditable instead of relying on an operator's memory of the previous notebook session.

teaching_blocks.title: Register and Package the Model
teaching_blocks.content: The serving package needs the fitted model and its fitted preprocessor together. A container that loads only weights or refits preprocessing can execute successfully without reproducing the intended prediction representation.

teaching_blocks.title: The working rule
teaching_blocks.content: Persist the fitted model and preprocessor together in the recorded version-tied package path. Import pickle, open that path with a binary "wb" handle and call pickle.dump on the dictionary {"model": model, "preprocessor": preprocessor}, passing the handle and protocol=5. Reload only a trusted, verified package in the compatible pinned inference environment. Open the package path with a binary "rb" handle and call pickle.load on that handle. Retrieve the model and preprocessor from the corresponding dictionary keys. Pickle loading can execute arbitrary code and is unsafe for untrusted artifacts. The Dockerfile uses FROM for the compatible Python image, WORKDIR /app, COPY requirements.txt ./ and RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt. COPY the package and serving source from the declared build context into their declared /app paths. Set CMD to the declared serving command and argument as a JSON array, so the default command loads this package. Replace source and command placeholders with the supplied package, inference dependencies and serving entry point.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Run docker build -t IMAGE:TAG CONTEXT to build and tag the package image; CONTEXT must contain the Dockerfile (or select it with -f) and every source used by COPY, with needed files not excluded by .dockerignore; record the resulting immutable image identity as well as its tag. The packaged prediction path must apply the fitted training preprocessing before the packaged model, not refit preprocessing at inference time. Use docker run --name NAME -p HOST_PORT:CONTAINER_PORT --env KEY=VALUE IMAGE to start the referenced image with the declared port and nonsecret runtime settings.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Inspect the named container with docker container inspect NAME to check its image identity and State fields. Use docker container logs NAME to inspect its captured standard output and error for initialization or execution failures. Do not embed secrets in Dockerfile ARG or ENV instructions, because they persist in the final image or its metadata.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Supply sensitive values through the runtime secret mechanism rather than placing their literal values in the Compose configuration. Save and reload the fitted model/preprocessor through explicit binary file handles, and write/read the pinned dependency manifest through a text file handle. Record pinned inference package versions in the package’s requirements manifest and install that manifest in the serving image.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Assert the pre-save and container-reloaded predictions agree on the same fixed inputs under declared tolerances, and separately check that fitted preprocessing parameters are preserved. teaching_blocks.title: Evaluate the Frozen Choice
teaching_blocks.content: The protected test is the final comparison for the already fixed system. Freeze candidate, preprocessing and threshold first; a disappointing test result must be reported rather than used to choose a replacement.

teaching_blocks.title: The working rule
teaching_blocks.content: Only evaluate the protected test set after fixing the selected candidate, fitted preprocessing and decision threshold; test results must not choose a replacement candidate or threshold. Generate selected-model and baseline predictions for the same protected-test observations and compare the precommitted predictive quantities on that cohort. Use the already fixed deployment class probabilities, error costs and operating requirements when computing the final comparison; report failure rather than retuning on the test.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: For binary validation counts, FPR = FP/(FP+TN) conditions on actual negatives, and FNR = FN/(FN+TP) conditions on actual positives; an empty conditioning group does not yield a defined rate. With zero cost for correct predictions and supplied deployment class probabilities, expected error cost is P(Y=0) × FPR × cost_FP + P(Y=1) × FNR × cost_FN.

teaching_blocks.title: A bounded work example

Use the already fixed deployment probabilities and error costs, not new values chosen to make B pass. Check the precommitted quality and operating requirements and retain the test's actual-class conditioning counts. If B fails the requirement, report failure. A threshold adjustment based on these test outcomes would let the protected observations choose the system, contradicting the boundary. The output is a final matched comparison, not another candidate-selection round.

Freeze means the choices are made before test outcomes are observed: model identity, fitted preprocessing, threshold, metric inputs and requirements all retain their declared values. The baseline and candidate predictions then use the same protected observations for a final matched comparison. Retain the test's observed conditioning counts while applying the supplied deployment probabilities; these are different roles in the calculation. If a required quantity is undefined or a requirement fails, report that outcome explicitly. This protects the interpretation of final testing rather than using it as a source of additional tuning information.

teaching_blocks.title: Monitor Distributions and Drift
teaching_blocks.content: Production-input summaries need a defined reference and measurement window. Compare the same representations and categories so an apparent change is not merely the result of different bins or different denominators.

teaching_blocks.title: The working rule
teaching_blocks.content: Compare captured production inputs with the defined reference dataset using the same feature representations, reference constraints and measurement window. For numerical values, np.histogram(values, bins=fixed_edges) returns bin counts; divide by the eligible observation count to compare bin proportions on the same edges. For categorical or predicted-class values, count each declared category and divide by its window total, retaining category definitions and the total count.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Record the production window, reference identity and observed summaries so an apparent distribution change can be investigated. Compute the arithmetic mean with np.mean(numeric_values) over the selected numeric observations. Compute standard deviation with np.std(numeric_values, ddof=0), which divides squared deviations by N before taking the square root; use ddof=1 only when the stated calculation requires the N−1 divisor.

teaching_blocks.title: A bounded work example
teaching_blocks.content:
Suppose the reference has category counts 60 and 40, while the production window has counts 30 and 70, each out of 100. Their aligned proportions are [0.60, 0.40] and [0.30, 0.70]. teaching_blocks.title: Monitor Distributions and Drift
teaching_blocks.content: An input distribution changed, but labels are not yet available. Distinguish evidence about inputs, evidence about the conditional target relationship and measured prediction quality before deciding what the observation supports.

teaching_blocks.title: The working rule
teaching_blocks.content: Input data drift is a change in the observed input distribution relative to its reference; input drift monitoring alone does not measure labeled prediction quality. Concept drift changes the conditional target relationship P(Y|X), that is, the relationship between features and labels; a previously useful model can become less useful as that relationship changes. Observed model quality degradation requires comparing predictions with corresponding ground-truth labels and the declared quality reference.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Without matched available labels, report the supported distribution or service evidence and the unresolved quality question rather than asserting labeled quality degradation. Input marginals describe P(X), conditional-target evidence describes P(Y|X), and matched-label errors describe observed quality; changing one does not logically establish changes in all three.

teaching_blocks.title: A bounded work example
teaching_blocks.content:
Suppose a production window contains more long-distance orders than the reference. That is evidence about P(X), the input distribution. It does not establish that P(Y|X), the target relationship conditional on features, changed. To claim observed quality degradation, compare predictions with their corresponding ground truth and the declared quality reference. If matched available labels are absent, record the supported distribution or service observation and the unresolved quality question. Conversely, a conditional target relationship can change in the concept-drift sense even when an input summary is not the evidence that reveals it. Keep the three questions distinct rather than calling every change ‘the model got worse.’

Separate an operational report into what is observed and what is unresolved. More long-distance inputs support an input-distribution statement. Matched labels compared with the quality reference support an observed-error statement. Conditional-target evidence addresses whether the feature/label relationship changed. The absence of labels does not prove that quality stayed constant; it means the labeled-quality question is not yet measured by that evidence. Likewise, input drift does not prove that quality worsened. Keeping these distinctions preserves uncertainty without discarding useful distribution or service evidence, and prevents a response justified by one type of evidence from being mislabeled as another.

teaching_blocks.content: Labels arrive after predictions. Keep the original prediction cohort and join by identity, so recent incomplete ground truth is not mistaken for a fully observed quality cohort.

teaching_blocks.title: The working rule
teaching_blocks.content: Use a prediction-ID dictionary to preserve cohort membership and prediction time before attaching delayed labels by key. teaching_blocks.content: Estimate P(label mature | cohort) as mature eligible prediction IDs divided by all eligible prediction IDs in that cohort, retaining the denominator. Compute the declared quality quantity on the matched mature cohort and report its label coverage; without justified coverage it does not estimate quality for all traffic. Compute the arithmetic mean with np.mean(numeric_values) over the selected numeric observations.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify

teaching_blocks.title: A bounded work example
teaching_blocks.content:
Suppose a fixed cohort contains 100 eligible prediction IDs, and 60 have matched mature labels under the declared delay and availability boundary. Label maturity coverage is 60/100 = 0.60. If six of those matched mature predictions are errors, their error proportion is 6/60 = 0.10, not 6/100. Retain the prediction-ID dictionary, timestamps and explicit handling of duplicate or unmatched labels. Compute required numerical summaries on the specified matched observations and report label coverage with quality. Without justified coverage, that mature-cohort result does not estimate quality for all traffic. Keep newer incomplete predictions distinguishable rather than treating their missing labels as successful outcomes.

Preserve cohort membership before labels arrive so later analysis cannot redefine the cohort around whichever predictions happened to receive labels. The availability boundary determines which matched labels are mature for this analysis. Duplicate labels or prediction IDs require explicit handling before the dictionary can conceal them. Report the 60 mature IDs and 100 eligible IDs alongside the six matched errors. The 0.10 result describes the mature matched cohort, while 0.60 describes its label coverage. These different ratios should not be merged into an all-traffic quality estimate without justified coverage evidence.

teaching_blocks.title: Labels, Alerts and Regression Diagnosis
teaching_blocks.content: A useful alert connects a defined indicator and window rule to an owner and response. Apply the supplied noise-tolerant rule to baseline evidence instead of alerting on every numerical fluctuation.

teaching_blocks.title: The working rule
teaching_blocks.content: Use the baseline measurement window and indicator definition to distinguish normal variability from an actionable breach. Write the existing alert’s indicator, threshold/window rule, owner and response in its YAML schema, then inspect the parsed configuration before replay. Apply the declared noise-tolerant threshold rule to the computed baseline mean/spread, rather than alerting on every single fluctuation.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Replay normal and breached windows, checking that only the configured breach produces the intended owner/action record. Compute the arithmetic mean with np.mean(numeric_values) over the selected numeric observations. Compute standard deviation with np.std(numeric_values, ddof=0), which divides squared deviations by N before taking the square root; use ddof=1 only when the stated calculation requires the N−1 divisor.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Write assert predicate checks for the declared valid, boundary and failure cases; a false predicate raises AssertionError during ordinary non-optimized execution. With the declared PyYAML dependency, import yaml; write a mapping/list configuration with yaml.safe_dump(config, file_handle), reload it with yaml.safe_load(file_handle), and inspect the required resolved fields before submitting it to the existing runtime. Safe loading accepts standard YAML tags, not arbitrary Python object constructors.

teaching_blocks.title: A bounded work example
teaching_blocks.content:
Suppose the existing policy names a baseline window, indicator, threshold rule and on-call owner. Compute its required mean and spread with the declared divisor, then write those policy fields into the existing YAML schema. Parse and inspect the resolved configuration before replay. A normal-window fixture should not create the breach owner/action record; a declared breached window should. Keep both fixture results so a correctly formatted alert that fires on every normal fluctuation does not pass the behavioral check. This exercise implements the supplied threshold rule, not a newly invented significance test or response policy.

The baseline statistics describe normal-window observations under the stated indicator definition; the threshold rule converts that evidence into the configured breach predicate. Keep those roles separate from ownership and response, which specify what happens after a qualifying breach. YAML round-trip inspection checks what the runtime will read, while replay checks what the alert actually emits. Both are needed: correctly spelled fields can still describe an overly noisy rule, and a correct predicate without an owner/action record is not the declared actionable outcome. Retain normal and breached replay evidence together.

teaching_blocks.title: Labels, Alerts and Regression Diagnosis
teaching_blocks.content: Client outcomes worsened after a release, but timing alone does not establish the cause. Triage the available release, schema, distribution, service and mature-label evidence, then test one supported hypothesis.

teaching_blocks.title: The working rule
teaching_blocks.content: Start triage with client-visible impact and the available timeline, deployment, data, service and quality evidence. A schema/value failure identifies data conditions to investigate, whereas a distribution difference alone does not prove labeled model-quality degradation. Compare the active artifact/configuration identities with the approved deployment and run record when investigating a release-correlated regression.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Check matched mature-label evidence before selecting a response justified specifically by prediction-quality degradation. Select the supplied supported action—data repair, approved rollback or gated retraining—under the existing incident policy and preserve the required validation gates. Calculate conditional labeled error rates for each release/cohort on matched eligible labels, keeping their conditioning counts distinct.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Reproduce and isolate the regression from the release/telemetry timeline, test one causal hypothesis against the evidence and choose only the supported response.

teaching_blocks.title: A bounded work example
teaching_blocks.content:
Compare active artifact/configuration identities with the approved deployment and run. If a schema fixture fails, investigate that data condition; if a distribution differs, do not equate it with measured labeled degradation. Calculate release/cohort error rates only on matched eligible mature labels, retaining distinct denominators. Reproduce and isolate the regression from the timeline and test one causal hypothesis. Choose only the policy-supported action justified by evidence: supplied data repair, approved rollback or gated retraining. Preserve required validation. A different class mix or incomplete labels cannot be silently treated as a causal model regression simply because they appeared after deployment.

Test the selected hypothesis against evidence that can distinguish it from alternatives. An artifact mismatch supports a different investigation from a schema defect, and neither is established merely by a distribution difference. Matched mature-label rates need their own release/cohort counts, so incomplete labels are not treated as successful predictions. Keep the incident response within the existing policy and its authorization boundary. After choosing the supported data repair, rollback or retraining path, preserve the corresponding validation gates and audit evidence. The diagnosis is bounded to the reproduced regression and available evidence rather than a blanket explanation of all model errors.

teaching_blocks.title: A distinction to keep

teaching_blocks.title: Execute Quality-Gated Retraining
teaching_blocks.content: Retraining can begin from a schedule, new data or supported operational evidence. The trigger should record why execution is eligible and which input it intends to use; it does not approve the future candidate.

teaching_blocks.title: The working rule
teaching_blocks.content: ML pipeline execution can be triggered by a schedule, availability of new training data, observed degradation of model performance or a significant change in data distribution. Choose the trigger supported by the supplied operational evidence, and retain the trigger reason and intended input dataset. Label-verified performance evidence and a distribution-only signal are different trigger evidence; do not describe drift alone as measured prediction error.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: A retraining trigger starts a gated pipeline; it does not by itself approve the resulting candidate for deployment. Reject unauthorized identities and uninvestigated alarm events at entry under the existing policy; preserve separate authorization for any later promotion. Annotate the existing data-quality/test, training and evaluation stages with their input artifacts and purpose, and make promotion depend on its own approval rather than retraining alone.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Trace one eligible event through the existing entry and required dependencies, then trace a failed check to show precisely which downstream stages cannot execute. Keep handoff credentials runtime-injected and out of the policy, YAML values and captured stage logs.

teaching_blocks.title: A bounded work example
teaching_blocks.content:
Suppose an investigated distribution signal satisfies the existing entry policy for an authorized identity. Record it as distribution evidence rather than labeled error, and bind the intended dataset. Annotate existing quality/test, training and evaluation stages with their artifact inputs and purposes. Trace the eligible event through required dependencies, then trace a failed data check to show where downstream execution stops. Test entry rejection for an unauthorized identity or an uninvestigated alarm. Keep later promotion dependent on its own approval. Handoff credentials remain runtime-injected and absent from policy values, YAML and captured logs.

A schedule event and a verified performance event may both be allowed trigger types, but their recorded reasons should retain the actual evidence used. Distribution-only evidence remains distribution-only even if it permits retraining under policy. Trace dataset identity across entry and quality checks so a permitted event cannot silently train on an unintended input. A failed required check blocks its downstream path; a completed retraining path still leaves promotion approval separate. The operational record should bind trigger reason, authorized identity, intended artifacts and dependency outcomes without exposing runtime credential values.

teaching_blocks.title: A distinction to keep
teaching_blocks.content: Retraining eligibility is not deployment approval. A distribution-only signal must not be relabeled as measured prediction degradation, and an alarm is not automatically an authorized trigger.

teaching_blocks.title: Execute Quality-Gated Retraining
teaching_blocks.content: Two workers receive the same retraining event, and one may restart after reservation or launch. The supplied durable coordinator must preserve one logical job identity across those cases while preventing overlap from a different run key.

teaching_blocks.title: The working rule
teaching_blocks.content: Read the declared run key and pipeline identity from the dictionary event record, and pass them to the supplied durable coordinator’s atomic admission operation. Use the supplied single atomic operation that reserves both the unique run key and pipeline active slot and persists the job ID; a process-local dictionary or separate check-then-write calls cannot supply that durable admission contract. Handle returned accepted, duplicate and busy statuses with explicit conditional branches: only an accepted reservation authorizes a new logical launch.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: For an accepted claim, invoke the executor with the reserved persisted job ID as its idempotency token; do not generate a replacement identity after a retry or restart. For a duplicate or restarted claim, resume or attach to that same persisted job identity; an unknown launch response requires same-token reconciliation rather than a second logical launch. For a busy slot held by a different run key, defer or reject under the supplied policy without launching an overlapping job.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Release the active pipeline slot only after confirmed terminal job state, retaining the completed run-key record so a later duplicate cannot relaunch it. Assert durable state and logical job count for two concurrent same-event workers, two different-key workers contending for one slot, and fresh workers after reservation and after launch. In an existing Cloud Build YAML/JSON configuration, each steps item declares its execution image in name and its command in args or script; wire the function/test entry point into the assigned stage.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Assign step IDs and set waitFor to the required preceding step IDs; downstream execution depends on those steps completing successfully, not just their textual location. Keep required gate failures fatal: do not set allowFailure or add failing gate exit codes to allowExitCodes, and ensure a rejected Python gate exits unsuccessfully. Use the configured Pub/Sub artifact/event trigger with its configured payload bindings and filters to run the existing pipeline, then inspect actual stage results and resolved inputs for accepted and rejected fixtures.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: With the declared PyYAML dependency, import yaml; write a mapping/list configuration with yaml.safe_dump(config, file_handle), reload it with yaml.safe_load(file_handle), and inspect the required resolved fields before submitting it to the existing runtime. Safe loading accepts standard YAML tags, not arbitrary Python object constructors.

teaching_blocks.title: A bounded work example
teaching_blocks.content: Pass run key K and pipeline identity to the single atomic admission operation. If accepted, use its persisted job ID J as the executor's idempotency token. A duplicate or restarted claim resumes or attaches to J; an unknown launch result is reconciled with that same token rather than replaced by J2. A different key facing the active slot follows the busy defer/reject policy without launching. Release the slot only after confirmed terminal state while retaining K's completed record. Test concurrent same-key workers, different-key contention and fresh workers after both reservation and launch, asserting durable state and logical job count. Keep required pipeline gates fatal.

teaching_blocks.title: A distinction to keep
teaching_blocks.content: A process-local dictionary or separate check-then-write calls cannot supply the durable atomic admission contract. A retry must not invent a new job identity, and releasing an active slot before terminal confirmation permits the wrong overlap.

teaching_blocks.title: Execute Quality-Gated Retraining
teaching_blocks.content: A retrained candidate is evaluated against the incumbent on a matched cohort. The validation result must bind the exact candidate identity and every required gate, not merely report aggregate improvement.

teaching_blocks.title: The working rule
teaching_blocks.content: Evaluate the retrained candidate and incumbent on the same declared validation cohort and compare them against the predeclared acceptance requirements. Use the supplied deployment class probabilities and error costs to calculate candidate and incumbent expected cost under the fixed selection rule. Reject a candidate that fails a required quality, slice or deployment-compatibility gate even if its aggregate validation score improves.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Bind the candidate’s exact registry/artifact identity and gate verdict to the controlled promotion record; validation of one artifact does not approve a different artifact. For binary validation counts, FPR = FP/(FP+TN) conditions on actual negatives, and FNR = FN/(FN+TP) conditions on actual positives; an empty conditioning group does not yield a defined rate. With zero cost for correct predictions and supplied deployment class probabilities, expected error cost is P(Y=0) × FPR × cost_FP + P(Y=1) × FNR × cost_FN.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Do not use protected test observations to fit preprocessing, choose a model or tune its settings; doing so leaks information into the chosen system. Write assert predicate checks for the declared valid, boundary and failure cases; a false predicate raises AssertionError during ordinary non-optimized execution.

teaching_blocks.title: A bounded work example
teaching_blocks.content:
Suppose the candidate has lower expected cost than the incumbent but fails a required slice check. Reject it under the fixed gate policy. Calculate both costs with the same supplied deployment probabilities, error costs and actual-class conditional rates. A missing conditioning group does not provide a defined rate. Keep protected-test observations out of fitting and setting choice. Bind the exact registry/artifact identity and verdict to the controlled promotion record, with assertion fixtures for accepted, boundary and failed cases. Approval evidence for candidate A must not be reused for candidate B just because both came from the same retraining pipeline.

The incumbent and candidate must be evaluated under the same fixed validation question before their expected costs are comparable. Keep quality, required slices and deployment compatibility as separately named gate results. A cost improvement does not erase a compatibility failure, and a complete gate record for one identity cannot be transferred to another. Accepted, boundary and rejected fixtures should verify both verdict and identity binding. Promotion evidence therefore states which exact candidate passed which requirements, rather than merely saying that the latest retraining run produced a model with a better number.

teaching_blocks.title: A distinction to keep
teaching_blocks.content: Retrained does not mean accepted. An aggregate gain cannot bypass a required slice or compatibility gate, and validation of one artifact does not approve another.

teaching_blocks.title: Use an ML Incident Runbook
teaching_blocks.content: The nonproduction runbook authorizes recovery of one identified service instance. Reproduce and isolate the injected fault, then test the supported recovery hypothesis before taking the lifecycle action.

teaching_blocks.title: The working rule
teaching_blocks.content: Use the nonproduction runbook and authorized recovery identity; reproduce and isolate the injected service fault and test one recovery hypothesis before the lifecycle action. Inspect instance status/identity and process/service state, recording fault evidence before recovery. Perform the runbook-approved gcloud compute instances stop INSTANCE --zone=ZONE, wait for completion, then start the same authorized instance and wait until it is running.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Reconnect with gcloud compute ssh INSTANCE --zone=ZONE and inspect the restored process/model service state. Verify model readiness and a bounded prediction exchange after restart, comparing the restored service behavior with the expected contract. Use existing runtime-injected credentials without embedding them in recovery code/configuration or printing them in captured output.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Use gcloud compute instances describe INSTANCE --zone=ZONE to inspect the instance status and identity before and after the authorized lifecycle action.

teaching_blocks.title: A bounded work example
teaching_blocks.content:
Inspect instance identity, state and process/service evidence and retain the fault record. Under the approved identity, stop the same authorized instance, wait, start it and wait until running. Reconnect and inspect the restored model service. Verify readiness and a bounded prediction exchange against the expected contract rather than assuming a running VM means recovery. Keep credentials in the existing runtime mechanism and out of commands, configuration and captured output. Record state before and after the action. This is a runbook-scoped nonproduction fixture, not permission to restart unrelated resources or broaden the recovery policy.

The pre-recovery evidence is important because stop/start can change process state and remove the immediate fault symptom. Inspect the authorized instance before acting, record what failed and test the runbook's supported hypothesis. After start completes, reconnect and compare model-service state and endpoint behavior with the expected contract. A running instance state is a lifecycle observation; readiness and a successful bounded prediction are service observations. Retain both in the same recovery record along with authorized target identity. This verifies the supplied recovery procedure without assuming that a restart of an arbitrary resource would be safe or sufficient.

teaching_blocks.title: A distinction to keep
teaching_blocks.content: Restarting a VM is not proof that model service behavior recovered. The authorized target, fault evidence and post-restart readiness/prediction checks all belong in the recovery verdict.

teaching_blocks.title: Control Workload Cost and Retire Resources
teaching_blocks.content: Resource telemetry must refer to the actual ML workload interval. Combining stopped intervals or unrelated processes with active measurements can produce a summary that no longer describes the workload you intended to inspect.

teaching_blocks.title: The working rule
teaching_blocks.content: Summarize CPU/memory telemetry over the defined ML workload window, retaining instance and process identity. Align resource measurements with instance start/stop states so stopped or unrelated intervals are not silently combined with active-workload utilization. Resolve process-state evidence against the running workload; for a containerized process, docker top shows running process state to compare with that evidence.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Compute descriptive CPU and memory utilization for the same matched workload interval and report observation count and units. Compute the arithmetic mean with np.mean(numeric_values) over the selected numeric observations. Compute standard deviation with np.std(numeric_values, ddof=0), which divides squared deviations by N before taking the square root; use ddof=1 only when the stated calculation requires the N−1 divisor.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Use gcloud compute instances describe INSTANCE --zone=ZONE to inspect the instance status and identity before and after the authorized lifecycle action.

teaching_blocks.title: A bounded work example
teaching_blocks.content:
Suppose the selected active interval has CPU observations 20, 40 and 60 percent. The mean is 40 percent and the ddof=0 standard deviation is about 16.33 percentage points. Retain the three-observation count and matched interval. Align memory measurements with the same instance and workload, and inspect lifecycle state before and after. For a containerized process, compare docker top evidence with the recorded running workload identity. Do not silently append an unrelated stopped interval to lower the apparent utilization. The result is descriptive CPU/memory evidence with units and process identity, not an execution-cost calculation.

Resource samples need both units and identity. CPU percent and memory units are not interchangeable columns, and their descriptive summaries should cover the same matched workload interval. The lifecycle record helps distinguish a stopped instance from an active measurement window. Process inspection adds evidence that the workload named in the report was actually running. Keep observation counts visible for both series and use the stated standard-deviation divisor. These summaries characterize resource usage during the bounded task; they do not independently establish billed cost, request success or model quality.

teaching_blocks.title: A distinction to keep
teaching_blocks.content: A low average is uninterpretable without its window and workload identity. Stopped or unrelated intervals must not be silently mixed into active-workload utilization.

teaching_blocks.title: Control Workload Cost and Retire Resources
teaching_blocks.content: Workload expenditure includes attributable direct and shared billing rows, not just time a training VM was computing. Select workload identities and reporting windows, then reconcile every eligible amount.

teaching_blocks.title: The working rule
teaching_blocks.content: Billing reports associate charges with services, resources and time intervals; select the declared training/inference workload and reporting window before comparing expenditure. Use the existing workload labels or resource-to-workload mapping to connect billed resource usage with the run or serving workload. Stopping a VM can end compute charges while persistent disks and other resources remain billable, so compute time alone does not account for all workload expenditure.

teaching_blocks.title: Apply and verify
teaching_blocks.content: Aggregate the supplied charge records by workload and charge category and reconcile the attributed total with the eligible record total. Calculate a declared unit-cost quantity from attributed expenditure divided by the corresponding completed work, retaining both the billing and work-measurement windows. Start and connect to both tagged instances for their bounded training/inference workloads, record their separate lifecycle windows, and stop both after execution.
